subject: Svenska 1
title: Language accuracy and sentence structure
sourceSummary: De and dem, incorrect word spacing (särskrivning), punctuation and run-on sentences — the mistakes that most often lower the grade on written assignments.

questions.opener: Try replacing the word with the English "they" or "them".
choices: Båda de och dem fungerar lika bra här.
Jag gav boken till de som satt längst bak.
Jag gav boken till dem som satt längst bak.
Jag gav boken till dom som satt längst bak i skriftspråk.
questions.explanation: After the preposition "till" ("to"), the object form is required: "dem". The test works: in English you say "to them", not "to they".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: "___ som kom sist fick stå upp."
questions.opener: Who is it that performs the action in the sentence?
questions.explanation: The word is the subject — it refers to those who came last. The subject form is "de" (compare "they came last", not "them came last").

questions.opener: A compound word is ONE concept — not two words that happen to stand next to each other.
choices: Sjukhuset är ett rök fritt område.
questions.explanation: "Rökfritt" ("smoke-free") is a compound word and is written as one word. Incorrect word spacing (särskrivning) often changes the meaning completely — compare "en brun hårig man" ("a brown, hairy man") with "en brunhårig man" ("a brown-haired man").

questions.prompt: "Jag läste boken, den var spännande." What is the problem with the sentence?
questions.opener: Count how many complete sentences have been squeezed together with just a comma.
choices: A run-on sentence (satsradning) — two main clauses are joined together with only a comma
questions.explanation: Two main clauses cannot be joined together with only a comma. Fix it with a full stop, a semicolon, or a conjunction: "Jag läste boken. Den var spännande." ("I read the book. It was exciting.") or "…boken, och den var spännande." ("...the book, and it was exciting.").

questions.prompt: When do you use a semicolon?
questions.opener: It lies midway in strength between two other punctuation marks.
choices: Instead of a comma in long sentences
Between two main clauses that are closely related
questions.explanation: A semicolon joins together two complete main clauses that are closely related: "Hon sa inget; hon behövde inte." ("She said nothing; she didn't need to.") A colon is used to introduce a list or a quotation.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
questions.opener: A colon points forward to something that explains or lists.
choices: Vi behöver: penna, papper och tid att arbeta.
Han sa: att han skulle komma senare.
Vi behöver tre saker: penna, papper och tid.
questions.explanation: A colon is used before a list, an explanation, or a quoted statement — but only when what precedes the colon is a complete clause. In the other options, the colon breaks in the middle of a clause.

questions.prompt: Correct the sentence and explain each change: "Läraren delade ut proven till de som var klara, många var nervösa dem hade inte hunnit plugga."
questions.opener: Look for three things: the wrong form of de/dem, a run-on sentence, and a sentence that needs to be split.
questions.answer: Läraren delade ut proven till dem som var klara. Många var nervösa; de hade inte hunnit plugga.
steps: "till de som var klara" → "till dem som var klara". After the preposition "till" ("to"), the object form is required.
"…var klara, många var nervösa" is a run-on sentence: two main clauses joined by only a comma. Put a full stop after "klara".
"många var nervösa dem hade inte hunnit plugga" has no punctuation at all. Insert a semicolon (or a full stop) between the main clauses.
"dem hade inte hunnit plugga" → "de hade inte hunnit plugga". Here the word is the subject — it refers to those who had not had time to study.

questions.prompt: What trick do you use to decide whether it should be "de" or "dem"?
questions.answer: Replace the word with the English they/them: if it becomes "they" you write "de", if it becomes "them" you write "dem". Alternatively, swap in vi/oss ("we"/"us"): "vi" → de, "oss" → dem. Short rule: "de" is the subject (the one doing something), "dem" is the object (the one something is done to) and always comes after a preposition.
